Company: Wooden furniture producer · Home country: Germany · Size: Large (250+ staff) · HS 940360 (Consumer goods) · Trade data 2019-2024

1. Executive Summary

Verdict: DO NOT ENTER NOW. Limited attractiveness at present; monitor and revisit.

Market attractiveness: 4.4/10
Recommended entry mode: Indirect / direct exporting via importers and distributors

  • Import market of $181.34 m in 2024, trend growth -14.8% a year (data confidence: high).
  • Supply is highly concentrated (HHI 2,437); top supplier Italy holds 45.77%.
  • CAGE distance from Germany: high.
  • Applicable import duty: 0% (MFN rate (no free-trade agreement)); landed cost ≈ +12% over ex-works price before VAT.
  • Germany is supplier #4 with 5.3% of imports, priced premium (3.79x market average per kg).
  • EU-27 suppliers hold 74.37% of China's imports.

Your starting position: Germany

  • Supplier #4 of 74 with 5.3% of imports in 2024 (+0.46 pp since 2019).
  • Price level: Premium, $26.12/kg vs a market average of $6.90/kg (3.79x).

4. PESTEL Analysis

  • Political: One-party state with active industrial policy (Made in China 2025, dual circulation). Geopolitical tension with the EU and US; retaliation risk in trade disputes (e.g. EU brandy, pork, dairy probes).
  • Economic: World's second-largest economy and a huge consumer market, but slower growth, weak consumer confidence and strong price competition from domestic champions. Latest: GDP growth 5.0% (2025), inflation 0.1% (World Bank).
  • Social: Digitally native consumers; 'guochao' preference for domestic brands among younger buyers; foreign brands win on safety, heritage and premium positioning.
  • Technological: World-leading e-commerce and super-apps (Tmall, JD, Douyin, WeChat); fast product cycles; strong domestic manufacturing capability.
  • Environmental: Dual-carbon goals (peak 2030, neutrality 2060) drive demand for clean-tech; growing ESG disclosure requirements.
  • Legal: Foreign Investment Law (2020) improved access; still complex licensing, local standards (GB/CCC), data-localisation rules and uneven IP enforcement.

5. CAGE Distance

Dimension Distance Evidence
Cultural High Different language families (Germanic vs Sinitic); localisation needed.
Administrative High No EU-China FTA: MFN tariffs, CCC/GB standards, distinct legal system and growing trade tension. Large governance gap (WGI +1.18 vs -0.11).
Geographic High ~7,358 km between capitals. Long lead times (Asia-Europe sea freight ~30-45 days; China-Europe rail ~15-20 days).
Economic High GDP per capita $60,496 (home) vs $13,862 (target), ratio 4.4x.

Overall distance: High.

6. Tariffs, Trade Defence & Regulation

Import duty

  • MFN applied tariff of China: 0%, 2023 (World Bank WITS / UNCTAD TRAINS (MFN applied, simple average)).
  • Likely rate for a company from Germany: 0% (MFN rate (no free-trade agreement)).

Goods (ex-works) 100.00

Regulatory checklist

  • CCC for listed products (e.g. toys); GB standards
  • Customs registration of the consignee; Chinese-language labelling for retail goods
  • Foreign Investment Law (2020) and the Negative List: most sectors open to wholly foreign-owned enterprises (WFOE)
  • Data Security Law and Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL) for any customer data collected
  • Cross-border e-commerce (e.g. Tmall Global, JD Worldwide) allows testing demand under a lighter regime for many consumer goods

Official texts: CNCA: China Compulsory Certification (CCC) · General Administration of Customs (GACC) · MOFCOM: foreign investment and the Negative List

Regulatory notes compiled 2026-11-21 from official sources; not legal advice.

Verify current duties and requirements: - China Customs tariff and regulations (GACC) - MOFCOM trade remedy notices - EU Access2Markets: China export requirements - EU SME Centre (China market guides)

7. Risk Matrix

Exchange rate (ECB reference rates): EUR per CNY: +3.1% over 2023-10–2026-10 (home currency weaker), annualised volatility 4.9%. Risk level: Low.

Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation
Dominant incumbent supplier (Italy, 45.77% share) High High Differentiate on quality, service, sustainability and EU/China-specific certification rather than price.
Shrinking import demand High Medium Target growing niches or member states; validate demand before fixed investment.
Trade-defence or retaliation measures in the EU-China corridor Medium High Monitor trade-defence notices; diversify sourcing and production locations; build tariff scenarios into pricing.
Institutional and IP-protection risk Medium High Register trademarks and patents locally before entry; use contracts with local arbitration (e.g. CIETAC/HKIAC).
Logistics disruption (Red Sea, port congestion, freight-rate swings) Medium Medium Use mixed sea/rail routing, safety stock in a regional hub, Incoterms that share freight risk.
Brand and message mis-fit with local consumers Medium Medium Local consumer testing, native-language content, local marketplace and social channels.
Currency volatility (EUR/CNY, 4.9% annualised volatility) Low Medium Price in home currency where possible; hedge large contracts with forwards.

8. Recommended Entry Mode

Indirect / direct exporting via importers and distributors

  • Moderate attractiveness or high distance favour a low-commitment, reversible entry.
  • Keeps capital at risk low while you learn the market.
  • Your home country already supplies 5.3% of this market (rank 4): existing importers and logistics routes lower the cost of entry, so partner with established importers first.
  • Home-country exports are priced above the market average: position on quality and brand, with selective distribution.
  • Inputs: attractiveness 4.4/10, CAGE distance high, institutional quality 4.8/10, company size large (250+ staff).

Sensitivity to the weights

The weights are a judgement call, so the same sub-scores are re-weighted under alternative schemes:

Weighting scheme Score
Base case 4.4
Equal weights 4.8
Size-led (large incumbents) 4.4
Growth-led (start-ups) 3.6

Niche entrant (openness first) 5.1

Weight-sensitive: the score ranges from 3.6 to 5.1 and crosses a verdict threshold (do not enter now, enter with caution), so treat the verdict as borderline.

10. 90-Day Action Plan

  1. Days 1-30, validate: confirm the HS code and duty rate on official tariff tools, size the niche with customer interviews, shortlist 10 potential partners or channels in China.
  2. Days 1-30, compliance: map required certifications and labelling (see section 6), get quotes from a test lab or regulatory agent, register trademarks in the target market.
  3. Days 31-60, commercial model: build a landed-cost and pricing model (duties, freight, VAT, channel margins, FX), and draft the partner or channel agreement.
  4. Days 31-60, go-to-market: localise product pages, packaging and sales material; pick 1-2 launch channels consistent with the entry mode: indirect / direct exporting via importers and distributors.
  5. Days 61-90, pilot: ship a pilot order or open the online store, track sell-through, margin and customer feedback against go/no-go KPIs.
